sources.title: Food security in Roman Palmyra (Syria) in light of paleoclimatological evidence and its historical implications
sources.access: Primary open-access publisher article, abstract and introduction read; DOI, authors and publication date verified
sources.used_for: Use hinterland production and food distribution as explicit constraints on a city-support scenario, while distinguishing local capacity from actual historical populations and political outcomes. No Palmyra yields, population figures or fitted coefficients transferred.

sources.title: The Grain Market in the Roman Empire: A Social, Political and Economic Study
sources.access: Primary Cambridge publisher introduction excerpt read; complete monograph not consulted
sources.used_for: Distinguish production, supply security and entitlement. Physical local food support does not establish access rights, actual staffing or sovereignty. No numerical parameters claimed from the book.

sources.title: Grain storage techniques: Factors influencing the choice of bulk store
sources.access: Primary manual storage discussion consulted during preceding storage milestone
sources.used_for: Carry forward separate finite rural, export and destination inventories. Storage durations and decay remain declared sensitivities, not measured ancient coefficients.

coefficient_status: All demographic requests, institutional cohorts, collection fractions, storage budgets and patrol ranges are explicit sensitivity assumptions. The literature motivates mechanisms and interpretation, not these coefficients.
